lead: A laser is chosen for a job by four numbers: wavelength, power, coherence and pulse length. Wavelength decides what absorbs the light. Power decides speed and depth. Coherence makes interference useful. Pulse length limits heat damage. These four numbers explain why a CO₂ laser cuts cloth but a semiconductor laser feeds a fibre link. Industry uses lasers to cut, weld and drill. Medicine uses them for eye and skin treatment. Communication uses them as fibre sources. Measurement uses them in rangefinders, interferometers and LIDAR, which is light detection and ranging. Shops use them in barcode scanners.
prereq: You need: 5.5 Semiconductor laser for the source, 5.4 for wavelength choice, and Unit 4 interference for measurement uses.

blocks.text: A laser is not chosen by name alone. Four properties decide the job: wavelength, power, coherence and pulse length. Wavelength is the colour or infrared line. Power is energy delivered per second. Coherence is how fixed the phase relation is across the beam. Pulse length is how long the light stays on. A cutter needs high average power and a spot that the material absorbs. A fibre link needs a small, fast semiconductor source. A hologram needs coherence. Eye surgery needs a pulse short enough to limit heat spread.

The same laser can serve different jobs when focused differently. A focused beam raises power density, the power per unit area, so material melts or vaporises. A broad beam heats a larger area. Pulsed operation gives high peak power with low average heating. This is why a pulsed Nd:YAG laser can break a membrane in the eye while a continuous CO₂ laser cuts cloth.

Material processing uses the laser as a controlled heat source. Cutting melts or vaporises a narrow line. Welding melts two edges so they join. Drilling makes a small hole, often in a hard material. CO₂ lasers at 10.6 µm cut cloth, wood and plastics. Nd:YAG lasers at 1064 nm weld and drill metals. The heat-affected zone is narrow because the energy arrives in a small spot for a short time. Indian sheet-metal shops use laser cutting for panels and enclosures.

Medicine uses the same idea with tissue. The wavelength must be absorbed by the target and not by unwanted tissue. Argon lasers at 488 nm and 514 nm are absorbed by blood and are used in retinal treatment. Nd:YAG at 1064 nm is used for posterior capsulotomy after cataract surgery. Excimer lasers at 193 nm shape the cornea. Dermatology uses pulsed dye lasers for vascular lesions and Nd:YAG for hair removal. Short pulses limit heat spread.

Consumer uses are common. A barcode scanner sweeps a low-power red laser diode or He-Ne beam across bars. Black bars absorb more and white gaps reflect more, so the reflected light carries the code. A laser printer writes an image on a photoconductor drum with a modulated beam. Optical storage uses a focused spot: CD at 780 nm, DVD at 650 nm and Blu-ray at 405 nm. Shorter wavelength gives a smaller spot and more data per disc.

Fibre communication uses a semiconductor laser as the source. The laser is modulated, meaning its output is switched or varied with the data. It couples into a fibre because its beam is narrow and bright. Silica fibre has low loss at 1310 nm and 1550 nm, so lasers at these wavelengths are common. A photodiode at the far end converts light back to current. Details of loss and repeaters are in 5.9.

Measurement uses coherence and timing. A laser rangefinder sends a pulse and times the echo. The pulse travels to the target and back, so distance is half the path. LIDAR scans a beam and measures many echo times to build a map. An interferometer splits a coherent beam into two paths and recombines them. A change in path length of one wavelength shifts the interference by one fringe. This measures small displacements; see Unit 4, interference.

blocks.where: d is distance to the target in metres; c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ is the speed of light; t is the echo time in seconds.

blocks.text: Spectroscopy uses a tunable dye laser or a narrow-line laser to probe absorption lines. Holography records the interference of an object beam and a reference beam; the theory belongs to Unit 4.

figure.caption: The four branches group laser jobs by what the user needs. Communication and measurement share one branch because both depend on coherence.

spec.aria: A tree groups laser applications into industry, medicine, communication and measurement, and consumer uses.

examples.question: A laser rangefinder sends a short pulse to a wall and receives the echo after 20.0 ns. Find the distance to the wall. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
steps: The pulse travels to the wall and back, so the path length is 2d.
Speed of light c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Time t = 20.0 ns = 20.0 × 10⁻⁹ s.
examples.check:
c = 3.00e8
t = 20.0e-9
path = c * t
d = path / 2
print(d)

traps: Missing the factor 1/2 in d = c t / 2 doubles every rangefinder distance.
Wavelength and power are not interchangeable. Short wavelength helps spot size in storage; high power helps cutting.
CO₂ at 10.6 µm and Nd:YAG at 1064 nm are infrared and invisible; a red He-Ne beam is visible.
A pulsed laser can have high peak power but low average power; average power is peak power times duty cycle.
Coherence is needed for interference, holography and interferometry; it is not the main reason a laser cuts steel.

quiz.q: Name three material-processing operations done with lasers.
Why does a short pulse reduce damage in laser surgery?
quiz.a: It limits the time for heat to spread, so nearby tissue stays cooler.

quiz.q: A laser pulse returns from a target after 40.0 ns. Find the distance. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Blu-ray uses 405 nm and CD uses 780 nm. Explain the storage difference.
quiz.a: A focused spot cannot be much smaller than about half the wavelength. 405 nm gives a smaller spot than 780 nm, so pits and tracks can be closer and more data fits on the disc.

quiz.q: Which wavelength band is used in low-loss silica fibre links?
Why is a coherent source needed for holography?
quiz.a: The object and reference beams must keep a fixed phase relation to form a stable interference pattern.

quiz.q: Find the photon energy of a 632.8 nm He-Ne laser. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
A student uses d = c t in a rangefinder and gets 6.0 m for t = 20.0 ns. What went wrong and what is the correct distance?
quiz.a: The pulse travels to the target and back, so c t is 2d. Dividing by 2 gives d = 3.0 m, not 6.0 m.

beyond: Not for the exam. Fibre lasers now dominate many cutting and welding shops because they are efficient and focus well. Ultrafast lasers with femtosecond pulses are used for precise glass and medical-device machining. LIDAR is moving from surveying to car safety and mapping. Search for fibre laser cutting, ultrafast laser micromachining, and LIDAR time of flight.
